Cluster 6 Investigation — PBMC Single-Cell RNA-seq Dataset

This report documents the completed investigation of Leiden cluster 6, a group of exactly 13 cells. The question was which biological expression program is supported by the available evidence, using UMAP position, quality control, enriched expression, comparisons with other clusters, per-cell consistency, raw counts, and alternative expression programs.

Evidence-based conclusion

Identity call: Platelet/megakaryocyte-associated expression program.

Cluster 6 forms a compact 13-cell group on the UMAP. Platelet/megakaryocyte-associated markers including PPBP, PF4, GP9, TUBB1, and RGS18 are enriched relative to other clusters and consistently detected across the cluster.

Alternative signal: CCL5 is detected across Cluster 6, but the tested T/NK-associated program is not comparably supported by canonical markers such as CD3D, GNLY, and NKG7. CCL5 alone is not treated as sufficient evidence for a T/NK identity.

Limitations and interpretation

  • Cluster 6 contains only 13 cells.
  • This supports an expression-program-based identity call rather than an absolute cell-type determination.
  • No external automated cell-type annotation method or dedicated doublet classifier was applied.
  • The results do not establish that the cells cannot be doublets.
  • UMAP separation alone does not establish biological identity.
  • The analysis does not establish that Cluster 6 is a novel population.
  • Interpretation depends on the genes and alternative programs examined.
  • This is one PBMC scRNA-seq dataset and should not automatically be generalized beyond it.

The supported wording is “platelet/megakaryocyte-associated expression program.” “Platelet-associated identity” is an evidence-supported interpretation of these data, not an absolute biological classification.

CCL5 and alternative interpretation

CCL5 is detected across Cluster 6, with mean normalized expression 4.2978 and detection in 13/13 cells. The canonical markers examined were not uniformly detected: CD3D was 0/13, GNLY was 0/13, NKG7 was 2/13, and CD3E was 2/13. The broader T/NK program therefore is not comparably supported by the tested canonical markers. This is a description of the measured pattern, not a contamination or doublet call.

Raw counts and doublets

Raw UMI counts from adata.layers["counts"] were inspected because simultaneous expression of different programs can motivate a doublet-related question. Raw counts preserve the individual-cell evidence but this report did not run a dedicated doublet-detection algorithm. No cell is classified as a doublet.

Figure 5. Raw counts for selected key genes across Cluster 6 cells. Zeros are valid measured values, not missing data.

From observation to conclusion

Cluster 6
→ compact UMAP group
→ QC inspected
→ platelet-associated markers enriched
→ signal reproduced across individual cells
→ signal stronger and more coherent relative to alternative programs
→ platelet/megakaryocyte-associated expression program supported

UMAP context contributes to the evidence chain, but it is not sufficient on its own.

Biological interpretation

The combined PPBP, PF4, GP9, TUBB1, and RGS18 pattern provides a coherent platelet/megakaryocyte-associated expression program. These genes are enriched in Cluster 6 relative to the other clusters and most are detected in 11–13 of the 13 cells. The broader per-cell pattern is more consistent with this program than with the alternative programs examined. CCL5 is an important observation requiring explicit discussion, but it is not interpreted alone as establishing a T/NK identity.

Understanding this analysis without a single-cell RNA-seq background

A. What single-cell RNA sequencing measures

DNA is the long-term genetic instruction set. RNA is produced when genes are being used; messenger RNA carries temporary copies of instructions into the cell's protein-making machinery. Single-cell RNA sequencing measures RNA molecules from individual cells. In the expression matrix, one row represents a cell and one column represents a gene; a value summarizes the detected expression of that gene in that cell.

B. What a marker gene is

A marker gene is a gene whose expression is characteristic of a cell type or cellular program. One gene can be noisy or shared, so a coherent combination is stronger evidence. Here, the joint PPBP/PF4/GP9/TUBB1/RGS18 pattern is more informative than any one gene alone.

C. What a cluster is

Cells are grouped computationally because their expression profiles are similar. Leiden cluster labels are computational group identifiers, not automatic biological names.

D. What UMAP is

UMAP compresses many-dimensional expression profiles into two dimensions for visualization. Each dot is a cell and nearby dots tend to have similar profiles. The axes have no direct biological meaning, and a separated island does not by itself prove a new cell type.

E. QC metrics

n_genes is the number of detected genes. Very low values can indicate limited RNA capture, while unusually high values can require inspection, but neither is definitive. total_counts is the total detected count signal; unusually high values can reflect more RNA, technical variation, or mixed material and require context. pct_mito is the percentage of signal associated with mitochondrial genes. High values are often inspected as a possible sign of stressed or damaged cells, but interpretation depends on the dataset.

F. Normalized expression vs raw counts

Normalized expression makes cells more comparable for expression-pattern analysis. Raw counts retain the original UMI-scale evidence and were inspected here for the question of simultaneous signals across individual cells.

G. Mean expression and fraction expressing

Mean expression describes the average amount of signal. Fraction expressing describes how many cells have a value above zero. A high mean can be driven by a subset, so both statistics matter.

H. Fold change

Fold change compares average expression between groups. A log2 fold change of one means a two-fold ratio; positive values indicate greater average expression in the first group and negative values indicate lower average expression.

I. Expression programs

An expression program is a transparent group of related genes summarized together. Identity is usually inferred more robustly from a coherent set than from one marker. The Cluster 6 platelet-associated program is the concrete example.

J. What a doublet is

A droplet can occasionally contain RNA from more than one cell. It may then show mixed signatures. Such co-expression can motivate investigation, but it does not prove a doublet; this report did not apply a dedicated classifier.

K. Plain-language conclusion

The 13 cells in Cluster 6 consistently express several genes characteristic of platelet/megakaryocyte biology. This pattern is stronger and more internally consistent than the alternative programs examined. Therefore the most supported interpretation is that Cluster 6 has a platelet/megakaryocyte-associated expression profile. Because the group is small and no external annotation or dedicated doublet analysis was performed, this is a well-supported evidence-based identity call rather than an absolute classification.
